clue.text: Verbosity adding weight at the end of the line

parts.note: padding is wordy filler stuffed into writing
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A long-winded speaker keeps piling on words right to the end of a line of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of the line' looks like the close of a line of print, but it is a railway line's terminus: PADDINGTON is a London mainline station where trains finish.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Paddington station is a terminus, the last stop where railway lines finish.

clue.text: Stick to artificial stone

explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a glue for sticking, and also a hard glass used to make imitation gems.

clue.text: Far from lively police patrols-—just down-and-outs

parts.note: dead is the opposite of lively
a police officer's beat is the route patrolled

explanation.surface: Officers on their rounds meet only listless tramps.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadbeat is an idle, penniless loafer, someone fallen on hard times.

clue.text: Burns the toast

parts.note: not a scorched slice of bread but the toast drunk to the poet Robert Burns at a Burns Night supper

explanation.walkthrough: At a Burns supper on 25 January, Scots honour the poet Robert Burns with a speech and toast by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The main speech and toast at a Burns supper honours the poet's lasting legacy under this title.

clue.text: Refuse to dress on time

parts.note: garb means clothing
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone declines to put on clothes in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is rubbish, the waste thrown away, which is a noun sense of refuse.

clue.text: Is against theatrical side and affectations

parts.note: OP is opposite prompt, the stage side facing the prompter
poses are affected attitudes

explanation.surface: Someone objects to the stage-side posturing of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: OP (opposite prompt) is the side of a British stage opposite the prompter's corner.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose is to resist or set oneself against something.

clue.text: Legal deeds

parts.note: read both as formal documents of law and as things done, deeds being actions

explanation.definitionFit: Statutes passed by a legislature are formal written instruments, and deeds in the everyday sense are actions or performances.

clue.text: One's after the pelt of this animal

indicators.note: after means the numeral is placed following the word for pelt

parts.note: an animal's pelt is its coat
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A hunter covets the fur of this creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's after' reads as 'one is after', placing I behind COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted raccoon relative of the Americas.

clue.text: The drama embraces even this town

indicators.note: embraces means one word holds the other inside its arms

parts.note: the stage means the theatre or drama as a profession

explanation.surface: A local theatre production finds a place even in this town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This town' is the definition; Stevenage is a post-war new town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is a town in Hertfordshire, England.

clue.text: Select Scottish town-documents with novel result

parts.note: to pick is to select
Wick is a town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland
papers are documents

explanation.surface: Choosing a Scottish town's records produces an unexpected outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pickwick Papers is Charles Dickens's first novel.

clue.text: Pretender has unusual medal given by King Edward

indicators.note: the word has is put into an unusual order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal, a British gallantry award
ER is Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher of a King Edward

explanation.surface: An impostor shows off a strange decoration supposedly presented by King Edward himself.
explanation.walkthrough: MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery, and ER is the royal cipher, Edwardus Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shams is faking, a pretender putting on a false show.

clue.text: But this soldier may frequent a public house

definitions.text: But this soldier may frequent a public house

parts.words: But this soldier may frequent a public house
parts.note: the lowest army rank shares its name with the opposite of public, so the clue plays on such a soldier drinking in a public house

explanation.definitionFit: The lowest-ranking soldier is called by the word that is the opposite of public, which the clue sets against the pub.

clue.text: When to take fast action with dying fires?

definitions.text: When to take fast action with dying fires?

parts.words: When to take fast action with dying fires?
parts.note: fast means going without food, not speed, and dying fires leave glowing remains, the name of these church fasting days

explanation.definitionFit: Ember days are four groups of three days in the church year set aside for fasting and prayer; dying fires leave embers.

clue.text: To which war is relentless

parts.note: the phrase war to the blade means a fight without mercy, and the clue asks what that blade is called

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom war to the knife means bitter, merciless conflict, so this blade completes the phrase.

clue.text: A help for her come-back

indicators.note: a come-back turns the phrase around, so the pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: the indefinite article written in its form before a vowel
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone offers a helping hand to a woman making her return.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'her': the answer is a woman's name, so it can stand for any woman so called.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is a woman's name, so any woman called that can be referred to as 'her'.

clue.text: Plant finger oo a list inconclusively

parts.note: a digit is a finger

indicators.note: without its conclusion, so the word list loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone points a finger at a plant on a list without reaching a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inconclusively' cuts the last letter, T, from LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis is the foxglove, a flowering plant also giving a heart drug.

clue.text: Assam, for example, has a capital dock road

definitions.text: Assam, for example, has a capital dock road

parts.words: Assam, for example, has a capital dock road
parts.note: Assam is a region in the east of the Indian subcontinent, and London, the capital, has a street named after that trade

explanation.definitionFit: Assam lies in eastern India, and London's East India Dock Road runs past the old docks of the trading company.

clue.text: Get South Indian MO to greedy Scot

parts.note: a medical officer is a doctor, abbreviated Dr
avid means eager or greedy
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A doctor is sent from southern India to treat a grasping Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dravidian peoples and languages, such as Tamil, are chiefly of southern India.

clue.text: Oval feature of fuel store

explanation.definitionFit: The Oval cricket ground in London is famous for the huge gas holders beside it, and a gas holder stores fuel gas.

clue.text: Seen over a door in a Roman street perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Something visible above an entrance in a street of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is the crossbar or small window placed above a doorway.

clue.text: Greek letter has low-down 0 on Aesop's fellow-slave

parts.note: rho is the Greek letter R
dope is inside information, the low-down

explanation.surface: A scholar reveals inside information about a slave who served with Aesop.
explanation.walkthrough: Herodotus says the courtesan Rhodopis was a slave together with Aesop, the fable writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodope, or Rhodopis, was the Thracian slave who served the same master as the fabulist.

clue.text: Kelvin and Evan back Jack

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

indicators.note: back means the name Evan is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Two men, Kelvin and Evan, are supporting their friend Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EVAN into NAVE; in cards the Jack is also called the knave.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of cards the jack is the alternative name for the knave.

clue.text: A hot unit, the Marines!

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A crack squad of Marines is described as a hot unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used for measuring gas supply.

clue.text: Gantry Lewis wrote about

parts.note: Gantry is not a crane frame but the surname of the preacher in Sinclair Lewis's novel, and his first name is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: Sinclair Lewis's 1927 novel is about a hypocritical preacher, and its title gives his full name.

clue.text: So wild a tornado, one is prostrated in it

indicators.note: a wild storm throws the letters about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tornado is so violent that a person throws themselves flat on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges A TORNADO together with I for one; worshippers lie prostrate in adoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is worship, and a worshipper may lie face down before the object of devotion.

clue.text: African ruler, for example, in students' union

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An African leader is cited as a case in a students' union debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus was the title of the emperor or king of Ethiopia.

clue.text: Point out these ghosts would be nocturnal creatures

indicators.note: taking this point out of the ghosts' name would leave the creatures, so the point sits inside the creatures' name

parts.note: lemurs are nocturnal primates of Madagascar
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone points out that these spooks are actually just animals that come out at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take the E out of the ghosts' name and it would be LEMURS, so the answer is LEMURS with E put in. The lemures were the restless spirits of the dead in Roman belief.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman religion the lemures were wandering spirits of the dead, placated at the festival of Lemuria.

clue.text: Time of opportunity locally

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance, and at the local, the neighbourhood pub, the important time is when the doors first unlock for drinkers

explanation.walkthrough: 'The local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub, which has fixed hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance or vacancy is an opening, and opening time is when a British pub starts serving.

clue.text: It's irrational and would make a seaman ridiculous

indicators.note: the answer would make the ridiculous word once the sailor is put in front, so the sailor is taken away from it

parts.note: absurd means ridiculous
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor is mocked as unreasonable and laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: an able seaman put in front of the answer would make a word meaning ridiculous, so the sailor is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a surd is an irrational root, such as the square root of two.

clue.text: Additional-signs of a Cockney picnic going to the beach

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the h at the start of words, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: hampers are the baskets packed for a picnic
sands means a beach

explanation.surface: A Londoner takes picnic baskets down to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney, a working-class Londoner, drops the H from HAMPERS. The ampersand is the & sign, read as 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the symbol & standing for 'and', a sign for adding something on.
